title: Shared offset, separate descriptor flags
purpose: Duplicate a close-on-exec descriptor, serialize two writes, and compare a zero-count read with a real read.
expected: ABCD with shared offset four; original CLOEXEC set and duplicate clear. Zero-count read leaves data available.
extension: Replace dup with a separate open before unlinking. Predict whether the second write overwrites. Restore immediate unlink after both opens succeed.
scope: One tiny mkstemp file, unlinked immediately; both descriptors close. Serialized regular-file operations, no durability claim.

title: Coalescing while blocked
purpose: Block SIGUSR1 before generating three instances, synchronously accept one, then probe for another without waiting.
expected: One SIGUSR1 accepted, then EAGAIN. The program never unblocks an unconsumed default-terminate SIGUSR1.
extension: Explain how a real-time signal and sigqueue would change counting, queue limits, and payload handling before implementing a bounded variant.
scope: Single-threaded process; signals target only itself. Original mask restored. Requires Linux sigtimedwait.

title: Copy, exit, reap
purpose: Change a child-local variable, return it through _exit, and decode the wait status in the parent.
expected: Parent local remains 7; child exits with 9; waitpid reaps exactly that child.
extension: Add an unlinked file descriptor before fork and compare shared file offset with the private C variable.
scope: One child, no recursive fork. Parent handles interrupted wait. Child runs no inherited stdio cleanup.

title: A bounded synchronized counter
purpose: Two joined workers each increment a counter 1,000 times under a mutex.
expected: Counter is exactly 2,000 after both joins. Thread scheduling order is unspecified.
extension: Move independent work outside the critical section and explain why the shared read-modify-write must remain protected. Do not use a data race as a valid benchmark.
scope: Two threads, fixed iteration counts, checked pthread return values, destroyed mutex; no detached work.

title: No writer is not the same as no bytes
purpose: Observe EAGAIN on an empty nonblocking pipe, then drain buffered data after closing its final writer.
expected: EAGAIN with live writer, XYZ after writer close, then zero for a positive-size read.
extension: Duplicate the write end and retain it after closing the original. Predict the last read and close the duplicate to restore EOF.
scope: One pipe, three bytes, nonblocking reader; both ends close. No packet-mode or multiple-reader behavior.

title: Private mapping, unchanged backing file
purpose: Change a private mapped byte and independently inspect the backing file with pread.
expected: Mapping contains Z at offset zero while file still contains A.
extension: Compare MAP_SHARED in a separate experiment and distinguish visibility from a crash-durability promise.
scope: Two-byte unlinked file and two-byte mapping; unmapped and closed. No concurrent truncation or SIGBUS experiment.

title: Stream half-close
purpose: Send six bytes over a local stream socketpair, half-close one direction, then send a reply in the other.
expected: All six bytes precede receive EOF; reverse reply OK still succeeds.
extension: Use a two-byte receive buffer and track framing independently from read boundaries. Explain why this does not exercise TCP TIME_WAIT.
scope: AF_UNIX socketpair, no network listener, six-byte payload and two-byte reply; both sockets close.

title: Partial drain after an edge
purpose: Register a nonblocking pipe with epoll edge notification, partially read it, then drain remaining bytes to EAGAIN.
expected: First event arrives; three bytes read, then five remain. Second zero-timeout poll is printed rather than used as a reservation.
extension: Compare level-triggered registration. Keep the actual read loop nonblocking in both cases.
scope: Linux epoll and pipe2; eight bytes; finite waits and watchdog; all descriptors close.

title: Timer expiration counter
purpose: Arm a 20 ms monotonic one-shot timerfd and consume its 64-bit expiration count.
expected: Count one; actual scheduling delay is not asserted or promised.
extension: Use a bounded periodic timer and delay reads. Explain why the counter can exceed one even though one read completes.
scope: Linux timerfd, one timer, one read, no wall-clock modification; descriptor closes.

title: Canonical input on a private PTY
purpose: Write a partial line at the master, observe an unreadable slave, then complete the line with newline.
expected: abc remains buffered until newline; slave returns abc plus newline. Echo is explicitly disabled.
extension: Set noncanonical mode with explicit VMIN and VTIME and predict readiness. Keep this private PTY separate from the user's interactive terminal.
scope: Linux devpts support, no shell child or controlling-terminal acquisition; both handles close and private PTY disappears.
